title: Research contexts
bodyHtml:
A research context is a loose model of a research area, collection of use cases, or scientific community. Research contexts vary in the hypotheses and questions considered most important, relative value placed on different data types, and familiarity with computational approaches. We have defined four research contexts to help users understand the information in the KC and its relevance to their research. More contexts, as well as the extent to which they customize the KC, are under development. Please contact us if you have suggestions for improving or adding contexts and capabilities to the KC.

Experimental biology

The experimental biology research context seeks to model research primarily interested in designing laboratory experiments that manipulate biomolecules, cells, or organisms to test a hypothesis regarding molecular, cellular, and physiological processes. Our model assumes that experimental biologists are primarily interested in using Common Fund data to conduct “look-ups” of their favorite biological entity (be it a gene, protein, or disease). It assumes that experimental biologists have limited exposure to sophisticated computational biology methods and have limited appetite for open-ended analysis and exploration of large-scale data.

Genetics

The genetics research context seeks to model research primarily interested in identifying naturally occurring genetic “experiments of nature” that provide causal and human-relevant links between molecular alterations and risk of disease. Our model assumes that geneticists are primarily interested in using Common Fund data to generate hypotheses regarding the molecular and cellular mechanisms that mediate an observed association between a variant or gene and a human trait. It assumes that geneticists have limited interest in data and analyses that cannot be mapped to or interrogated by genetic variants, but they are willing to conduct their own data analyses if a hypothesis suggested by the KC precomputed analyses is of sufficient interest.

Drug development

The drug development research context seeks to model research primarily interested in developing novel drugs that can modulate the activity of a gene or protein to prevent or treat human disease. Our model assumes that drug developers are interested in using Common Fund data to both generate new hypotheses and also test existing hypotheses regarding disease biomarkers and subtypes, as well as candidate drug targets. We assume that they are relatively computationally fluent, find value in quick “look-ups” of information for hypothesis testing, and are also willing to conduct their own data analyses if a hypothesis suggested by the KC precomputed analyses is of sufficient interest.

Computational biology

The computational biology research context seeks to model research primarily interested in reusing, integrating, and mining large biological datasets to generate new hypotheses regarding a broad range of biological processes. Our model assumes that computational biologists find limited value in simple web-interfaces and are more interested in accessing data for open-ended exploration and analyses.
